propositions: Snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot process; every other host that resolves attested gates populates the snapshot store but never reclaims it, causing unbounded growth.

The GC trigger must avoid the long-lock pitfall by performing an O(1) in-process check on the gate-resolution tail with no ticket-store lock, deferring heavy work to a detached child off the critical path.

The trigger must use stamped worker-lock and last-pass-stamp sidecars keyed on the snapshot store root to achieve single-flight across simultaneous hosts/worktrees and tolerate harmless overlap with the review-bot's resident janitor.
A detached child process runs the existing run_gc policy under its own flock, with durable cwd anchored at the snapshot store root and stdio detached to avoid inheriting ephemeral worktree state.
Attested gate resolution is the single choke point that must invoke maybe_gc; the trigger is disabled when interval_seconds <= 0 and never raises into the calling gate operation.
